title: bilingual credit factsheet live workbook
instruction:
You are Eamon Wainwright, the financial analyst supporting Meadowgate Housing Trust's global credit strategy, and Florian Mikkelsen needs this quarter's reusable production workbook ready for the product review meeting. Ashcombe Provisions distributes the strategy through Québec branches and expects the quarterly factsheet and commentary to look like its own established publication, with English and French pages mirroring one another. Use the supplied file `ashcombe_last_quarter_factsheet.xlsx` as the only edition reference. Build `ashcombe_quarterly_factsheet_workbook.xlsx` in the top level of the working directory. This is a live workbook for preparing the current quarter, not a pasted mock-up: leave all current-quarter input cells, commentary text areas, and calculated result displays empty until figures and approved wording are entered, but make the calculation and review affordances work when the inputs are supplied. Keep the established exhibit order and labels from the reference, retain the fixed bilingual grid, and allow the attribution table to accept nine sector rows even though the previous edition showed six. Put the English and French versions on separate printable sheets with matching page structure, and keep every French figure linked to the same underlying value as its English counterpart. The workbook should make it easy to identify missing inputs, out-of-range percentages, and disagreements between the two language pages without relying on a reviewer to compare cells by eye. Include a short user guide explaining the intended entry areas, the treatment you chose for the expanded sector coverage, and the review checks before release. The sector selector must use the exact controlled choices supplied in the reference workbook, and the workbook must retain the reference terminology rather than inventing new product labels. Use formulas wherever a value can be derived, preserve a visible distinction between editable inputs and calculated cells, and do not invent performance figures, holdings, dates, approvals, logos, or commentary. It will be printed for branch distribution, so set the English and French sheets up to print as matching one-page-wide pages with readable bilingual copy and no clipped table boundary. Do not add extra deliverables or rename the file.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/ashcombe_last_quarter_factsheet.xlsx` — The sole edition reference: it supplies the prior factsheet's exhibit order, labels, bilingual terminology, six-sector attribution structure, controlled sector vocabulary, recurring disclaimer language, and print conventions to be carried forward conservatively.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `ashcombe_quarterly_factsheet_workbook.xlsx` — A blank-but-live bilingual quarterly factsheet production workbook containing a guide, shared inputs, and matching English and French printable sheets. (Write the file at the top level of the solver's starting working directory using exactly this filename.; The workbook must contain sheets named Guide, Inputs, English, and Français, in that order.; Current-quarter inputs and narrative fields must remain blank; formulas, validations, conditional formatting, labels, and review instructions may be populated.; English and French pages must use the same underlying input values and equivalent exhibit structure.; No external links, macros, invented figures, invented commentary, logos, or additional files.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

sheets.name: Guide
rows: Ashcombe Provisions | Quarterly factsheet production guide
Prepare the current-quarter bilingual factsheet for branch print distribution. Complete Inputs first; English and Français are printable output pages.
Enter the quarter-end date, fund name, returns and sector figures only in the yellow cells on Inputs. Green cells are formulas or linked displays and should not be overwritten.
Use the dropdown in each Sector row. It contains only the controlled choices carried from the previous edition; do not type a new classification.

The prior edition displayed six sectors. This production grid reserves nine rows. Use only supplied current-quarter sectors from the controlled list; leave unsupported or unused rows blank and do not infer classifications.
Red warnings identify missing required entries, weights outside 0%–100%, and completed portfolio or benchmark weights that do not total 100%. Resolve them before release.
Write approved English and French commentary in the bordered yellow areas on their respective pages. Do not state a figure or conclusion that is not supported by the entered data and approved review.

□ Required inputs complete  □ Portfolio and benchmark totals reviewed  □ English/French numeric agreement confirmed  □ Commentary supported and approved  □ Print preview confirms both pages fit and table borders are visible
Both language pages link to the same Inputs values. If a display looks different, use the review warning and check the shared input rather than editing either page.

spec.professional_context: This is a quarterly reporting workbook for a credit strategy distributed through Ashcombe Provisions, with Meadowgate Housing Trust responsible for producing a branch-ready bilingual factsheet for internal product and distribution stakeholders. The work combines portfolio attribution, controlled commentary drafting, and print-oriented bilingual production.
difficulty_sources: The supplied edition uses a six-sector attribution grid while the reusable quarter-end instrument must accommodate nine sectors.
French copy is expected to run longer than the corresponding English copy, creating a practical trade-off between bilingual alignment and readable presentation.
The workbook must preserve numerical lineage and reusable calculation logic rather than merely displaying pasted answers.
The source edition does not fully specify how to handle the expanded sector set, so the analyst must make and document a conservative bounded judgment.

source_construction.content: Create one realistic prior-quarter edition workbook containing the established exhibit order, English and French labels, six populated sector rows, the controlled sector list, recurring disclaimer text, and print conventions. Use synthetic but internally consistent values and names. The six displayed sectors must be a subset of the controlled list; the new workbook will reserve nine rows without requiring the solver to invent sector names.

review_checks: portfolio and benchmark weight totals not equal to 100% when complete
English/French displayed values not linked to the same source

must_include: documented conservative treatment of the six-to-nine-sector expansion
warning that commentary must not be written as an unsupported figure

english_sheet.purpose: Printable English factsheet and commentary page.

table.boundary_row: A21:F21 is the total row immediately following the nine sector rows.
formula_requirements: displayed sector figures link to Inputs rather than duplicated constants
total row sums the nine sector rows
headline return and benchmark comparison link to Inputs
commentary figure callouts, where present, link to the same shared values

french_sheet.purpose: Printable French counterpart with the same exhibits and page geometry.
requirements: same exhibit order and table dimensions as English
all numeric displays linked to Inputs or the corresponding English source values
French narrative areas blank at delivery
French labels and recurring terminology taken from the reference

live_affordances: data validation dropdown on each sector input cell
conditional formatting for missing required entries and invalid percentage totals
formula cells visibly distinguished from editable cells
defined names for the shared sector table and key headline inputs
print area, page size, orientation, fit-to-width, and repeated header settings on both language sheets

print_geometry.language_sheets: Each prints to exactly one page wide and one page tall using the reference edition's paper size and orientation.
print_geometry.mirroring: English and French have matching print areas, exhibit boundaries, and table row/column geometry.
print_geometry.physical_use: Pages are printed separately and placed side by side or distributed as a bilingual branch handout; no clipped rightmost column or total-row border.

Validate formulas, defined names, validation lists, conditional formatting, print settings, sheet order, blank-entry behavior, and rendered page geometry offline using openpyxl and pypdf. Confirm that formulas return blank displays when inputs are blank and that all rubric predicates are observable from the submitted workbook.
